qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: QQQ ETF franchise provides a liquidity network effect and brand recognition, but legacy active equity and multi-asset strategies suffer from persistent net outflows and relentless industry fee compression. 10-year median GAAP ROIC is 6.8% (well below the 12% hurdle) and GAAP ROIC plunged negative in 2025 due to a $1.8B intangible impairment. Invesco has zero pricing power to outpace inflation, as passive index competition forces fee yields continually downward.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC = 6.8% < 12%, zero pricing power, REJECT). While Invesco holds a dominant ETF franchise in the Invesco QQQ Trust with strong liquidity network effects, its broader business is burdened by secular active mutual fund outflows, value-destructive legacy M&A (e.g. OppenheimerFunds write-downs), and relentless industry fee compression. 10-year median GAAP ROIC of 6.8% fails the 12% hurdle, and net management fee yields continue to decline across the cycle.
qualitative.evidence: 10-year median GAAP ROIC is ~6.8%, failing the 12% hurdle. In 2025, GAAP operating margin fell to -10.9% and net income was severely negative due to a $1.8B non-cash intangible asset impairment (primarily goodwill/intangibles from the OppenheimerFunds acquisition). While Free Cash Flow was positive ($1.12B in 2024 and $1.44B in 2025), total debt remains substantial at ~$9.78B at year-end 2025. Invesco faces structural secular headwinds from passive fee compression and active fund outflows, negating pricing power above inflation.
